findings.evidence: Private declarations occur at lines 35, 125, 255, and 271. Their hypotheses concern arbitrary nonnegative product integrands, Gaussian linear forms, independent MGFs, and independent mean-zero coordinates with finite second moments, respectively.
findings.fix: Relocate and export integrable_and_integral_prod_le, integral_exp_mul_dotProduct_pi_gaussianReal, mgf_sum_le_of_iIndepFun, and integral_star_dotProduct_mulVec_eq_sum_diag_aux in their integration, Gaussian, and moment infrastructure modules.
findings.issue: General integration, Gaussian, and moment results are private, making consumers repeat proofs unrelated to Hanson–Wright.

findings.evidence: The private theorem at line 94 assumes only Y ≥ 0 almost everywhere and E[exp(Y/B)] ≤ 2; neither its statement nor proof requires sub-Gaussianity.
findings.fix: Export this result in general exponential-moment infrastructure and use it to derive the squared sub-Gaussian specialization.
findings.issue: mgf_sub_integral_le_of_nonneg_exp_le_two hides a general sub-exponential estimate; the public square-specific theorem cannot serve arbitrary nonnegative variables with an exponential moment.

findings.evidence: Lines 97–103 prove that w ↦ (w i, w j) preserves the corresponding product marginals for i ≠ j, using only product-measure independence and evaluation identities.
findings.fix: Relocate and export the evaluation-pair measure-preserving theorem alongside product-measure evaluation results.
findings.issue: measurePreserving_eval_pair is private despite being general finite-product measure infrastructure.

summary: Reusable infrastructure is hidden behind private declarations, preventing consumers from using results under their actual, weaker hypotheses.
